title: QuickBooks Accounting
description: A full 14-module QuickBooks program from beginner to advanced: setting up a company file, the chart of accounts, customers and invoicing, payments and deposits, vendors and bills, bank feeds and reconciliation, inventory, payroll, sales tax, financial statements, budgets, closing the books, hands-on projects and a Certificate of Completion.
outcomes: Set up a QuickBooks company file correctly, from settings to opening balances
Build and maintain a chart of accounts that answers real management questions
Raise invoices, receive payments, and manage customers, estimates and credit notes
Record bills, expenses, cheques, purchase orders and vendor credits
Use bank feeds, rules and matching, and reconcile an account to the statement
Track products, services and inventory, and understand FIFO valuation
Run payroll, record deductions as liabilities and remit them on time
Configure and file sales tax, and avoid the errors that cause arrears
Produce and interpret the Profit and Loss, Balance Sheet and cash flow statement
Post journals, build budgets, track by class, and close the books at year end
about: QuickBooks is the accounting software used by millions of small businesses, NGOs, churches and freelance bookkeepers worldwide. Knowing it well is one of the most directly employable finance skills available.

This course teaches QuickBooks in the order the work actually happens: set the file up, record money in, record money out, reconcile the bank, then report and close. Every lesson pairs a short video with a full written teaching note and a practice quiz.
It is written for Liberian learners, entrepreneurs, office staff, NGO and church administrators, and anyone who wants to keep books that a bank, a funder or a tax authority will accept.
requirements: No QuickBooks experience required, this course starts from account creation
A phone or computer with a browser and an internet connection for the videos
A free QuickBooks trial or the Intuit sample company for practice
Basic arithmetic and a willingness to repeat each lesson in the software

faqs.answer: The course teaches QuickBooks Online, but the accounting concepts are identical in Desktop and only the menus differ.

faqs.answer: Yes. Complete the lessons, quizzes and final assessment to earn a verifiable TIH Professional Certificate.

lessons.title: 1.1 Welcome to the QuickBooks Course
lessons.html:
QuickBooks AccountingModule 1: Getting Started with QuickBooks

LESSON NOTE: WELCOME TO THE QUICKBOOKS COURSE

SubjectTopicLevelLesson duration
QuickBooks AccountingWelcome to the QuickBooks CourseBeginner to Advanced30 minutes

Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you should be able to:

  • Explain what this course covers and the order the topics are taught in
  • Describe the kind of work a QuickBooks user actually does each week
  • Set up the practice habit that makes the software stick

1. Introduction

QuickBooks is the accounting program used by millions of small businesses, NGOs, churches and freelance bookkeepers around the world. It does not replace accounting knowledge; it speeds up the recording work so you spend your time reading the numbers instead of copying them.

This course takes you from opening an account for the first time to closing the books at year end. Every lesson is one focused idea plus a short video, so you can learn on a phone, on limited data, a lesson at a time.

2. What this course covers

The course follows the real order of work in a QuickBooks file:

StageModulesWhat you learn
Set up1 – 3Create the file, configure settings, build the chart of accounts
Money in4 – 5Customers, invoices, payments and deposits
Money out6Vendors, bills, expenses and cheques
Reconcile7Bank feeds, rules and matching the bank statement
Specialised8 – 10Inventory, payroll and sales tax
Report and close11 – 12Financial statements, budgets and year-end
Prove it13 – 14Practical projects, assessments and the capstone

3. How to study this course

Watching is not learning. The learners who finish able to use QuickBooks all do the same three things:

  1. Watch the lesson video once without touching anything.
  2. Open a free QuickBooks trial or the sample company and repeat the steps yourself.
  3. Answer the practice quiz before moving on, and write down anything you got wrong.
Note: If you cannot open QuickBooks yet, still do the written exercises on paper. The thinking is the part that transfers; the clicking is the easy part.

4. What you need

  • A phone, tablet or computer with a browser
  • An internet connection for the videos (they can be watched at low quality)
  • A notebook for the exercises
  • Optionally, a free 30-day QuickBooks Online trial or the Intuit sample company

Summary

  • The course moves in the same order as real work: set up, money in, money out, reconcile, report, close.
  • QuickBooks speeds up recording; it does not replace understanding.
  • Repeat each lesson in the software yourself before moving on.

Key Terms

TermMeaning
QuickBooksAccounting software used to record income, expenses and produce financial reports.
CapstoneThe final practical project where you build a complete QuickBooks file.
Sample companyA free practice file Intuit provides so you can click freely without damaging real data.

Review Questions

Multiple choice

What is the main benefit of using QuickBooks over paper records?

  1. It records and organises transactions quickly so you can spend time interpreting the numbers
  2. It removes the need to understand accounting at all
  3. It guarantees a business will make a profit
  4. It files your taxes automatically without any input
Show answer

Answer: A. QuickBooks speeds up the recording work; interpretation and accounting judgement still belong to you.

In what order does this course teach QuickBooks?

  1. Set up, money in, money out, reconcile, report, close
  2. Year-end first, then setup
  3. Payroll first, then everything else
  4. Reports first, then data entry
Show answer

Answer: A. The course deliberately follows the real sequence of work in a live QuickBooks file.

What is the recommended way to study each lesson?

  1. Watch, repeat the steps yourself, then answer the quiz
  2. Watch the video twice and move on
  3. Read only the summary
  4. Skip to the assessments
Show answer

Answer: A. Repeating the steps yourself is what turns watching into a usable skill.

Why does the course suggest using a sample company file?

  1. It lets you practise freely without damaging real business data
  2. It is the only place reports can be produced
  3. Real company files cannot record transactions
  4. It is required before you can buy QuickBooks
Show answer

Answer: A. A sample file is a safe sandbox: mistakes there cost nothing.

Short answer

Name the six stages this course moves through.

Model answer

Set up; money in; money out; reconcile; specialised areas such as inventory, payroll and sales tax; report and close.

Why is watching a lesson video not enough on its own?

Model answer

Because the skill is in doing the steps. Repeating them in the software turns passive watching into something you can actually perform at work.

Class Activity

  1. Write down the name of a real organisation (your business, church, or a shop you know) and list the money coming in and going out in a typical week.
  2. Sign up for a free QuickBooks trial or open the Intuit sample company and simply look around for ten minutes without changing anything.

Assignment

In one page, describe the organisation whose books you will keep during this course. State what it sells or does, roughly how many transactions it has in a month, and who needs to see its financial reports.

lessons.title: 1.2 What Is QuickBooks?
lessons.html:
QuickBooks AccountingModule 1: Getting Started with QuickBooks

LESSON NOTE: WHAT IS QUICKBOOKS?

SubjectTopicLevelLesson duration
QuickBooks AccountingWhat Is QuickBooks?Beginner to Advanced35 minutes

Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you should be able to:

  • Define QuickBooks and state what it is used for
  • Distinguish what QuickBooks does automatically from what the user must decide
  • Identify the main areas of the program

1. Introduction

Every organisation that handles money has to answer three questions: What came in? What went out? What is left? QuickBooks is a tool built to answer those three questions quickly and consistently.

2. Meaning

QuickBooks: Accounting software made by Intuit that records financial transactions, stores them in a structured ledger, and produces financial reports from them.

The important phrase is structured ledger. When you type an invoice into QuickBooks you are not writing a note; you are creating a double-entry accounting record that instantly updates the customer's balance, the sales figure and the profit report.

3. What QuickBooks does for you

QuickBooks does this automaticallyYou still have to decide this
Posts the debit and the credit for each transactionWhich account a transaction belongs to
Keeps a running balance for every accountWhether a cost is an expense or an asset
Adds up reports instantlyWhether the numbers look reasonable
Downloads transactions from the bankWhether a downloaded item is really what it appears to be
Calculates sales tax on an invoiceWhether that customer or item is actually taxable
Note: This table is the honest summary of the whole course. QuickBooks removes the arithmetic, not the judgement.

4. The main areas of the program

  • Dashboard — a summary of cash, income and expenses
  • Sales — customers, invoices, estimates, payments received
  • Expenses — vendors, bills, expenses, cheques
  • Banking — downloaded transactions, rules, reconciliation
  • Reports — profit and loss, balance sheet, cash flow and dozens more
  • Settings — how this particular company file behaves

5. Who uses it

Small business owners keep their own books in it. Bookkeepers keep several clients' books in it. Accountants review and adjust it at year end. Because all three can look at the same file, QuickBooks is often the shared language between an owner and their accountant.

Summary

  • QuickBooks records transactions as proper double-entry accounting records, not just notes.
  • It automates arithmetic and posting; the user still supplies the judgement.
  • Its main areas are Dashboard, Sales, Expenses, Banking, Reports and Settings.

Key Terms

TermMeaning
IntuitThe company that makes QuickBooks.
LedgerThe structured store of all accounting records.
Double-entryThe rule that every transaction affects at least two accounts, with debits equal to credits.

Review Questions

Multiple choice

What does QuickBooks create when you enter an invoice?

  1. A double-entry accounting record that updates several accounts at once
  2. A plain text note with no accounting effect
  3. Only a printed page for the customer
  4. A tax return
Show answer

Answer: A. Entering an invoice posts a real accounting entry, updating the customer balance, sales and profit.

Which of these does QuickBooks NOT do for you?

  1. Decide which account a transaction belongs to
  2. Calculate the running balance of an account
  3. Add up a profit and loss report
  4. Post the debit and credit of a transaction
Show answer

Answer: A. Choosing the correct account is a judgement call that remains the user's responsibility.

Where would you go to see customers and invoices?

  1. The Sales area
  2. The Banking area
  3. The Settings area
  4. The Reports area only
Show answer

Answer: A. Customers, invoices, estimates and payments received all live under Sales.

Why is QuickBooks often described as a shared language between an owner and an accountant?

  1. Both can work in the same file, so the accountant reviews exactly what the owner recorded
  2. Because it translates between different languages
  3. Because accountants cannot use any other software
  4. Because owners are not allowed to see the reports
Show answer

Answer: A. A single shared file means the accountant reviews and adjusts the very records the owner entered.

Short answer

Give two things QuickBooks automates and two things it cannot decide for you.

Model answer

Automates: posting debits and credits, and totalling reports. Cannot decide: which account a transaction belongs to, and whether a figure looks reasonable.

Explain in your own words what a 'structured ledger' means.

Model answer

It means each entry is stored as a proper accounting record in named accounts, so the software can total and report on it, rather than being free text.

Class Activity

  1. List five transactions from a small shop and, for each, name the area of QuickBooks you would use to record it.
  2. Open the Dashboard of a sample company and write down every figure you can see and what you think it means.

Assignment

Write a short explanation, for someone who has never used accounting software, of what QuickBooks is and what it cannot do for them. Keep it under 200 words and avoid jargon.

Printable: use your browser’s Print → Save as PDF to keep an offline copy.

lessons.title: 1.3 QuickBooks Online vs QuickBooks Desktop
lessons.html:
QuickBooks AccountingModule 1: Getting Started with QuickBooks

LESSON NOTE: QUICKBOOKS ONLINE VS QUICKBOOKS DESKTOP

SubjectTopicLevelLesson duration
QuickBooks AccountingQuickBooks Online vs QuickBooks DesktopBeginner to Advanced35 minutes

Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you should be able to:

  • State the main differences between QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Desktop
  • Choose the right version for a given organisation
  • Explain why this course teaches QuickBooks Online

1. Introduction

QuickBooks comes in two quite different products that share a name. Choosing wrongly is expensive and awkward to undo, so it is worth ten minutes of thought before you sign up for anything.

2. The two products

QuickBooks OnlineQuickBooks Desktop
Where it runsIn a web browser, on any deviceInstalled on one Windows computer
AccessAnywhere with internetOnly at that computer, unless hosted
PaymentMonthly subscriptionAnnual licence
BackupsAutomatic, held by IntuitYour responsibility
Multiple usersBuilt in, from anywhereNeeds a network setup
Works offlineNoYes
Best forMost small organisations, mobile users, shared access with an accountantHeavy inventory or industry-specific needs, poor internet

3. Choosing between them

Ask three questions:

  1. Do several people need access from different places? If yes, Online.
  2. Is your internet unreliable? If yes, Desktop deserves a serious look.
  3. Do you have complex manufacturing or industry-specific inventory needs? If yes, Desktop's advanced editions may fit better.
Example: A church treasurer in Monrovia who wants the pastor and the auditor to see the books from their own phones should choose Online. A hardware wholesaler tracking assembled goods on one office computer with weak internet may be better on Desktop.

4. Why this course uses QuickBooks Online

Online needs no installation, runs on a phone, is what most new users are sold today, and lets a learner in any country open the same screens shown in the videos. Almost every concept in this course — the chart of accounts, invoices, reconciliation, reports — is identical in both products; only the menus differ.

Summary

  • Online runs in a browser on any device; Desktop installs on one Windows computer.
  • Online is a subscription with automatic backups; Desktop is a licence and you handle backups.
  • Choose Desktop mainly for unreliable internet or heavy industry-specific inventory.
  • The accounting concepts are the same in both; only navigation differs.

Key Terms

TermMeaning
SubscriptionA recurring monthly or yearly payment for continued access to software.
LicenceA one-off purchase giving the right to use a specific version.
HostingPaying a provider to run Desktop on a remote server so it can be reached online.

Review Questions

Multiple choice

Which version runs in a web browser on any device?

  1. QuickBooks Online
  2. QuickBooks Desktop
  3. Both run only on Windows
  4. Neither
Show answer

Answer: A. QuickBooks Online is browser-based and works on phones, tablets and computers.

An organisation has very unreliable internet. Which version deserves closer consideration?

  1. QuickBooks Desktop, because it works offline
  2. QuickBooks Online, because it is cheaper
  3. Neither can be used
  4. Only the mobile app
Show answer

Answer: A. Desktop works offline, which matters most where connectivity is poor.

Who is responsible for backups in QuickBooks Desktop?

  1. The user
  2. Intuit
  3. The bank
  4. The customer
Show answer

Answer: A. Desktop backups are the user's responsibility; Online backs up automatically.

Why do the accounting concepts transfer between the two versions?

  1. Both record the same double-entry accounting; only the menus differ
  2. Because they share one database
  3. Because Desktop is a copy of Online
  4. They do not transfer at all
Show answer

Answer: A. The underlying accounting is identical, so skills carry across; only navigation changes.

Short answer

Give two reasons a small NGO with several remote staff should pick QuickBooks Online.

Model answer

Staff can access it from anywhere on any device, and multi-user access plus automatic backups are built in.

Why is choosing the wrong version costly?

Model answer

Moving data between the two products is awkward and can lose detail, and you may have already paid for a licence or subscription you cannot use.

Class Activity

  1. Interview or imagine two organisations and recommend a version for each, giving two reasons per recommendation.
  2. Write down the three questions from this lesson and answer them for your own organisation.

Assignment

Write a one-page recommendation for a business of your choice, stating which QuickBooks version they should use and defending the choice against the strongest argument for the other version.

Printable: use your browser’s Print → Save as PDF to keep an offline copy.

lessons.title: 1.4 Choosing the Right QuickBooks Plan
lessons.html:
QuickBooks AccountingModule 1: Getting Started with QuickBooks

LESSON NOTE: CHOOSING THE RIGHT QUICKBOOKS PLAN

SubjectTopicLevelLesson duration
QuickBooks AccountingChoosing the Right QuickBooks PlanBeginner to Advanced30 minutes

Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you should be able to:

  • Compare the main QuickBooks Online plans
  • Match a plan to an organisation's real needs
  • Avoid paying for features you will never use

1. Introduction

QuickBooks Online is sold in tiers. Each tier adds features and cost. Most small organisations overpay because they buy on the feature list rather than on what they actually do each month.

2. The tiers, in plain terms

PlanAddsTypical fit
Simple StartInvoices, expenses, basic reports, 1 userA sole trader or freelancer
EssentialsBills, multi-currency, 3 usersA small business paying suppliers on credit
PlusInventory, projects, budgets, class tracking, 5 usersA shop with stock, or an NGO tracking projects
AdvancedMore users, deeper reporting, workflow automationA larger organisation with several departments
Note: Tier names and prices change between countries and years. Judge by the feature you need, not the name.

3. How to choose without overpaying

Work from your actual transactions, not ambitions:

  1. Do you sell stock you must count? If yes you need Plus for inventory.
  2. Do you receive supplier bills to pay later? If yes you need Essentials or above.
  3. Do you need to report by project, branch or funder? That is class/location tracking, so Plus.
  4. How many people must log in? Count real logins, not staff.
Example: An NGO with three programme funders needs Plus, because reporting spend per funder needs class tracking — even though it holds no inventory at all.

4. Upgrading later

You can move up a tier at any time and your data stays intact. Moving down can be restricted, and features such as inventory quantities may be lost. So start at the tier you need now, not the one you might need in three years.

Summary

  • Plans differ by features and user count, not by accounting quality.
  • Inventory and class tracking usually force the Plus tier.
  • Upgrading later is easy; downgrading can lose data, so do not overbuy.

Key Terms

TermMeaning
TierA pricing level of the same software with a different feature set.
Class trackingTagging transactions so income and cost can be reported by project, branch or funder.
User seatOne person's login, usually counted against the plan limit.

Review Questions

Multiple choice

Which requirement usually forces an organisation onto the Plus plan?

  1. Tracking inventory quantities or reporting by project
  2. Sending a single invoice
  3. Having one user
  4. Printing a report
Show answer

Answer: A. Inventory and class/project tracking are Plus-tier features.

Why should you avoid buying a higher tier than you need?

  1. You pay monthly for features you never use
  2. Higher tiers keep worse records
  3. Higher tiers cannot be upgraded
  4. Reports are less accurate
Show answer

Answer: A. The accounting is the same; you would simply be paying for unused features.

An NGO must report spending separately for three funders. What feature does it need?

  1. Class or location tracking
  2. Inventory valuation
  3. Multi-currency
  4. Payroll
Show answer

Answer: A. Class or location tracking tags each transaction so spend can be reported per funder.

What is the risk of downgrading a plan later?

  1. Some features and their data, such as inventory quantities, can be lost
  2. Nothing at all changes
  3. The company file is deleted
  4. Reports become unavailable forever
Show answer

Answer: A. Downgrading can be restricted and may strip features whose data then cannot be kept.

Short answer

List the four questions that decide a plan.

Model answer

Do you hold stock? Do you receive bills to pay later? Do you report by project/branch/funder? How many people must log in?

Why is the accounting quality the same on every tier?

Model answer

Every tier records the same double-entry transactions; tiers only differ in which extra features and how many users are available.

Class Activity

  1. Pick a real organisation and decide its tier using the four questions, writing one line of justification each.
  2. Find the current QuickBooks pricing page for your country and note what each tier costs per month.

Assignment

Recommend a plan for a shop that holds stock, employs two office staff who both need logins, and buys goods on credit from suppliers. Justify each feature you say they need.

Printable: use your browser’s Print → Save as PDF to keep an offline copy.

lessons.title: 1.5 Creating Your QuickBooks Account
lessons.html:
QuickBooks AccountingModule 1: Getting Started with QuickBooks

LESSON NOTE: CREATING YOUR QUICKBOOKS ACCOUNT

SubjectTopicLevelLesson duration
QuickBooks AccountingCreating Your QuickBooks AccountBeginner to Advanced35 minutes

Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you should be able to:

  • Create a QuickBooks Online account or trial
  • Enter the initial company details correctly
  • Explain why the first few answers matter later

1. Introduction

Signing up takes five minutes, but three of the answers you give during sign-up quietly shape the whole file: your industry, your business type and your start date. Getting them right now saves rework later.

2. The sign-up steps

  1. Go to the QuickBooks website and choose a plan or the free trial.
  2. Create an Intuit account with an email address you will keep — this becomes your login and cannot be casually swapped.
  3. Enter the business name exactly as it should appear on invoices.
  4. Choose the industry. QuickBooks uses this to suggest a starting chart of accounts.
  5. Choose the business type (sole trader, partnership, company, non-profit). This affects the equity accounts created.
  6. State what you want to track — this switches optional features on or off.

3. Why those answers matter

AnswerWhat it silently controls
IndustryThe suggested chart of accounts you start with
Business typeWhich equity accounts exist (Owner's Equity vs Retained Earnings)
Start dateThe date from which you will enter transactions and opening balances
EmailYour permanent login and where all notifications go
Note: None of these are permanent prison sentences — most can be changed in Settings — but changing them after you have entered hundreds of transactions is far more work.

4. Choosing a start date

The cleanest start date is the first day of a financial year or the first day of a month. Everything before that date is entered once as opening balances; everything after it is entered as normal transactions. Starting mid-month means you must split a bank statement, which is avoidable pain.

Summary

  • Sign-up answers for industry, business type and start date shape the file.
  • Use an email address you will keep — it becomes your permanent login.
  • Start on the first day of a month or financial year to keep opening balances clean.

Key Terms

TermMeaning
Intuit accountThe login that owns your QuickBooks subscription.
Start dateThe date from which transactions are recorded in the file.
Opening balanceThe balance of an account on the start date, carried in from the old system.

Review Questions

Multiple choice

Why should the start date be the first day of a month or year?

  1. Everything before it becomes a single opening balance, avoiding split statements
  2. Because QuickBooks refuses other dates
  3. Because reports only run monthly
  4. It makes the subscription cheaper
Show answer

Answer: A. A clean cut-off means you never have to split a bank statement between two systems.

What does the industry answer control?

  1. The suggested chart of accounts you begin with
  2. Your subscription price
  3. The number of users allowed
  4. Your tax rate
Show answer

Answer: A. QuickBooks proposes a starting chart of accounts based on the industry chosen.

Why does the email address used at sign-up matter?

  1. It becomes the permanent login and receives all notifications
  2. It appears on every invoice
  3. It sets the currency
  4. It determines the fiscal year
Show answer

Answer: A. The Intuit account email is your login, so it should be one you will keep access to.

What does the business type affect?

  1. Which equity accounts are created, such as Owner's Equity or Retained Earnings
  2. The colour of the dashboard
  3. The number of reports available
  4. Whether invoices can be sent
Show answer

Answer: A. Equity is structured differently for a sole trader, a company and a non-profit.

Short answer

Name three sign-up answers that are hard to change later and say why.

Model answer

Industry, business type and start date — they shape the chart of accounts, the equity accounts and the point from which transactions exist, so changing them after data entry means rework.

What is an opening balance?

Model answer

The balance an account already had on the file's start date, brought in from the previous records so the new file starts from the true position.

Class Activity

  1. Open a free trial and complete sign-up for a practice organisation, writing down each answer you gave.
  2. Decide the ideal start date for an organisation you know and explain your choice in two sentences.

Assignment

Create a practice QuickBooks account (or write out the answers you would give). Record your chosen industry, business type and start date, and explain in a paragraph what each one will affect.

Printable: use your browser’s Print → Save as PDF to keep an offline copy.

lessons.title: 1.6 Touring the QuickBooks Dashboard
lessons.html:
QuickBooks AccountingModule 1: Getting Started with QuickBooks

LESSON NOTE: TOURING THE QUICKBOOKS DASHBOARD

SubjectTopicLevelLesson duration
QuickBooks AccountingTouring the QuickBooks DashboardBeginner to Advanced30 minutes

Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you should be able to:

  • Identify each part of the QuickBooks dashboard
  • Read the dashboard summaries correctly
  • Know which dashboard figures can mislead you

1. Introduction

The dashboard is the first screen you see. It is a summary, not a report — it is designed to tell you at a glance whether anything needs attention today.

2. The main panels

PanelWhat it showsWhat to do with it
Cash flow / Bank accountsBalance in QuickBooks vs balance at the bankIf the two differ a lot, transactions are unrecorded
InvoicesUnpaid, overdue and recently paidChase anything in the overdue band
ExpensesSpending by category for the periodSpot a category that has jumped unexpectedly
Profit and LossIncome minus expenses for the periodA quick health check, not a final figure
SalesRecent sales trendCompare against the same period last year

3. Reading it honestly

Two traps catch new users:

  • The bank figure is not your cash. The 'in QuickBooks' balance excludes cheques not yet cashed and transactions you have not categorised yet.
  • The dashboard profit is provisional. Until bills are entered and the month is reconciled, profit usually looks better than it is.
Note: Treat the dashboard as a smoke alarm: useful for noticing a problem, useless for measuring it. Use the Reports area to measure.

4. Customising what you see

Most panels can be switched to different date ranges, and the whole dashboard can be set to show only the accounts you care about. Set the period to this month for daily use and this year when reviewing performance.

Summary

  • The dashboard is a summary and early-warning screen, not a report.
  • A gap between the QuickBooks and bank balances means unrecorded transactions.
  • Dashboard profit is provisional until bills are entered and the month reconciled.

Key Terms

TermMeaning
DashboardThe summary home screen of QuickBooks.
OverdueAn invoice past its due date and still unpaid.
Provisional figureA number that will change once all records for the period are complete.

Review Questions

Multiple choice

What does a large gap between the QuickBooks balance and the bank balance usually mean?

  1. Some transactions have not been recorded or categorised yet
  2. The bank has made an error
  3. The dashboard is broken
  4. Profit is too high
Show answer

Answer: A. The gap is normally unrecorded or uncategorised activity, not a bank mistake.

Why is dashboard profit described as provisional?

  1. Unentered bills and unreconciled items mean it usually looks better than reality
  2. Because it is always wrong
  3. Because profit cannot be measured
  4. Because it only counts cash sales
Show answer

Answer: A. Until every bill is entered and the month reconciled, expenses are understated.

What is the dashboard best used for?

  1. Noticing that something needs attention
  2. Producing the final financial statements
  3. Filing tax returns
  4. Recording invoices
Show answer

Answer: A. It is an early-warning summary; measurement belongs in the Reports area.

Which panel would you check to chase money owed to you?

  1. Invoices
  2. Expenses
  3. Sales tax
  4. Payroll
Show answer

Answer: A. The Invoices panel shows unpaid and overdue customer invoices.

Short answer

Give the 'smoke alarm' analogy for the dashboard in your own words.

Model answer

It warns you that something may be wrong so you go and look properly, but it does not measure the size of the problem — reports do that.

Name two things excluded from the 'in QuickBooks' bank figure.

Model answer

Cheques written but not yet cashed, and downloaded transactions that have not been categorised.

Class Activity

  1. Open a sample company dashboard and write down every panel and one decision it could prompt.
  2. Change the dashboard period from this month to this year and note which figures change most.

Assignment

Take a screenshot or sketch of a dashboard and annotate each panel, stating what it shows and one action a manager might take because of it.

lessons.title: 1.7 Navigating Menus and Settings
lessons.html:
QuickBooks AccountingModule 1: Getting Started with QuickBooks

LESSON NOTE: NAVIGATING MENUS AND SETTINGS

SubjectTopicLevelLesson duration
QuickBooks AccountingNavigating Menus and SettingsBeginner to Advanced30 minutes

Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you should be able to:

  • Move confidently around the QuickBooks menus
  • Use the +New button to create any transaction
  • Find any setting quickly

1. Introduction

Almost every 'I cannot find it' problem in QuickBooks is a navigation problem, not a knowledge problem. Learn three controls and you can reach anything.

2. The three controls that matter

ControlWhereWhat it does
+ NewTop leftCreates any transaction: invoice, bill, expense, deposit, journal entry
Left navigationDown the sideMoves between areas: Sales, Expenses, Banking, Reports, Payroll
Gear / SettingsTop rightAll configuration: account settings, chart of accounts, users, products, tools
Note: If you remember nothing else: + New creates, the Gear configures, the left bar navigates.

3. The +New menu, grouped

The +New menu is organised in four columns that mirror accounting itself:

  • Customers — invoice, payment received, sales receipt, estimate, credit memo
  • Vendors — expense, cheque, bill, pay bills, purchase order
  • Employees — payroll items
  • Other — bank deposit, transfer, journal entry, reconcile

Notice the pattern: money in on the left, money out next to it. If you can classify a transaction, you can find its form.

4. Finding a setting fast

  1. Click the Gear icon.
  2. The menu is grouped as Your Company, Lists, Tools and Profile.
  3. Almost every configuration question is answered under Account and settings (company-wide behaviour) or Chart of accounts (where things post).
Example: To change the invoice number format: Gear → Account and settings → Sales → Sales form content.

Summary

  • + New creates transactions; the Gear configures the company; the left bar navigates areas.
  • The +New menu is grouped as Customers, Vendors, Employees and Other.
  • Most configuration lives under Account and settings or Chart of accounts.

Key Terms

TermMeaning
+ NewThe universal create button for all transactions.
Gear iconThe settings menu for the whole company file.
Left navigationThe sidebar that switches between functional areas.

Review Questions

Multiple choice

Which control do you use to create an invoice?

  1. + New
  2. The Gear icon
  3. The Reports tab
  4. The Dashboard
Show answer

Answer: A. + New creates every kind of transaction, including invoices.

Where are company-wide configuration options found?

  1. Under the Gear icon
  2. Under + New
  3. On the dashboard
  4. In the Reports area
Show answer

Answer: A. The Gear icon opens settings for the whole company file.

How is the + New menu organised?

  1. By Customers, Vendors, Employees and Other
  2. Alphabetically
  3. By date created
  4. By amount
Show answer

Answer: A. It is grouped to mirror who the transaction involves, which makes forms easy to find.

You want to change how invoice numbers are formatted. Where do you go?

  1. Gear → Account and settings → Sales
  2. + New → Invoice
  3. Banking → Rules
  4. Reports → Sales
Show answer

Answer: A. Sales form behaviour is configured in Account and settings under Sales.

Short answer

State the one-line rule for the three main controls.

Model answer

+ New creates, the Gear configures, and the left bar navigates.

Why is the + New menu grouped the way it is?

Model answer

Because it mirrors who the transaction involves — customers, vendors, employees or other — so if you can classify the transaction you can find its form.

Class Activity

  1. Open + New and write down every form listed, grouped under its heading.
  2. Using only the Gear icon, find and note where you would change the company name, add a user, and view the chart of accounts.

Assignment

Write a one-page 'navigation cheat sheet' for a new colleague, showing where to go for the ten most common tasks in QuickBooks.

Printable: use your browser’s Print → Save as PDF to keep an offline copy.

lessons.title: 1.8 How QuickBooks Uses Double-Entry
lessons.html:
QuickBooks AccountingModule 1: Getting Started with QuickBooks

LESSON NOTE: HOW QUICKBOOKS USES DOUBLE-ENTRY

SubjectTopicLevelLesson duration
QuickBooks AccountingHow QuickBooks Uses Double-EntryBeginner to Advanced45 minutes

Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you should be able to:

  • Explain double-entry bookkeeping in plain language
  • Show the two sides QuickBooks posts for common transactions
  • Read the journal behind any QuickBooks form

1. Introduction

QuickBooks hides accounting behind friendly forms, but underneath every invoice and expense is a double-entry journal. Once you can see that journal, QuickBooks stops being mysterious and starts being predictable.

2. Meaning

Double-entry bookkeeping: The rule that every transaction is recorded in at least two accounts, with total debits always equal to total credits.

The logic is simple: money never appears from nowhere. If cash increases, something must explain it — a sale, a loan, an owner's contribution. Double-entry forces you to name that explanation.

3. What QuickBooks posts behind each form

You enterDebit (what increased)Credit (source)
Invoice to a customerAccounts ReceivableSales income
Payment receivedBank / Undeposited FundsAccounts Receivable
Bill from a supplierExpense accountAccounts Payable
Paying that billAccounts PayableBank
Cash expenseExpense accountBank
Owner puts money inBankOwner's Equity
Note: Read the table twice. Nearly every confusion later in this course — 'why is my profit wrong?', 'why does the customer still show a balance?' — is answered by one of these six lines.

4. Why invoicing does not increase cash

A common shock for new users: you raise a $500 invoice and profit goes up, but the bank does not move. That is correct. The invoice debits Accounts Receivable (a promise to pay), not the bank. Cash only moves when the payment is received.

Example: Raise a $500 invoice: Debit Accounts Receivable $500, Credit Sales $500. Customer pays: Debit Bank $500, Credit Accounts Receivable $500. Sales was recorded once, not twice.

5. Seeing the journal yourself

On almost any saved transaction you can open More → Transaction journal and QuickBooks will show you the exact debits and credits it posted. Use this whenever a report surprises you; it is the fastest way to learn what a form really does.

Summary

  • Every QuickBooks form posts a double-entry journal with equal debits and credits.
  • An invoice debits Accounts Receivable and credits Sales; cash moves only on payment.
  • Transaction journal on any saved form reveals exactly what was posted.

Key Terms

TermMeaning
DebitThe left side of an entry; increases assets and expenses.
CreditThe right side of an entry; increases income, liabilities and equity.
Accounts ReceivableMoney customers owe you.
Transaction journalA QuickBooks view showing the debits and credits behind a form.

Review Questions

Multiple choice

What does QuickBooks post when you raise a customer invoice?

  1. Debit Accounts Receivable, credit Sales income
  2. Debit Bank, credit Sales
  3. Debit Sales, credit Bank
  4. Debit Accounts Payable, credit Bank
Show answer

Answer: A. An invoice creates a receivable and records the income; no cash moves yet.

Why does the bank balance not change when you raise an invoice?

  1. Because the invoice records a promise to pay, not a cash movement
  2. Because QuickBooks has a delay
  3. Because invoices are not accounting records
  4. Because the sale is cancelled
Show answer

Answer: A. Cash only moves when the customer actually pays, which is a separate entry.

In double-entry, what must always be true?

  1. Total debits equal total credits
  2. Debits must exceed credits
  3. Only one account is affected
  4. Cash must always increase
Show answer

Answer: A. Equal debits and credits is the defining rule of double-entry.

Where can you see the exact debits and credits behind a saved QuickBooks form?

  1. More → Transaction journal
  2. The Dashboard
  3. Account and settings
  4. The Banking feed
Show answer

Answer: A. Transaction journal reveals the posting QuickBooks made for that form.

Short answer

Write the two entries for invoicing a customer $200 and later receiving payment.

Model answer

Invoice: Debit Accounts Receivable $200, Credit Sales $200. Payment: Debit Bank $200, Credit Accounts Receivable $200.

Why does double-entry stop money 'appearing from nowhere'?

Model answer

Because every increase must be matched by a named source, so each transaction carries its own explanation.

Class Activity

  1. For five everyday transactions in a shop, write the debit and credit QuickBooks would post.
  2. Open any saved transaction in a sample company and view its Transaction journal; write down what you see.

Assignment

Take ten transactions from a small business and produce a two-column table showing the debit and credit QuickBooks would record for each. Mark which ones change the bank balance.

Printable: use your browser’s Print → Save as PDF to keep an offline copy.

lessons.title: 2.1 Company Settings and Preferences
lessons.html:
QuickBooks AccountingModule 2: Setting Up Your Company File

LESSON NOTE: COMPANY SETTINGS AND PREFERENCES

SubjectTopicLevelLesson duration
QuickBooks AccountingCompany Settings and PreferencesBeginner to Advanced35 minutes

Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you should be able to:

  • Locate and change company-wide settings
  • Explain what each settings tab controls
  • Set a new file up so later data entry is consistent

1. Introduction

Settings decide how QuickBooks behaves for everyone using the file. Five minutes here prevents months of inconsistent data entry.

2. The settings tabs

TabControls
CompanyName, address, contact details, logo, tax number
Billing & subscriptionYour plan and payment
UsageHow close you are to plan limits
SalesInvoice layout, terms, fields shown, discounts, deposits
ExpensesBills, purchase orders, default payment terms
PaymentsHow customers can pay you online
TimeTimesheet options
AdvancedFiscal year, accounting method, closing date, currency, categories

3. The settings that matter most

  • Accounting method (Advanced) — cash or accrual. This changes every report.
  • First month of fiscal year (Advanced) — decides where your year starts.
  • Default terms (Sales) — sets when invoices become overdue.
  • Closing date (Advanced) — locks past periods so nobody edits closed months.
Note: Set the accounting method and fiscal year before entering data. Changing them later silently restates every report you have already produced.

4. Worked setup

Example: A Monrovia retailer: Company tab — name and TIN; Sales tab — default terms Net 15, discount field on; Advanced — fiscal year starts January, accrual accounting, closing date set after each month is reconciled.

Summary

  • Settings are company-wide and shape how everyone enters data.
  • Accounting method and fiscal year must be set before data entry.
  • A closing date protects reconciled periods from later edits.

Key Terms

TermMeaning
Accounting methodWhether income and expenses are recorded when cash moves (cash) or when earned/incurred (accrual).
Fiscal yearThe twelve-month period the financial statements cover.
Closing dateA date before which transactions cannot be changed without a password.

Review Questions

Multiple choice

Which setting changes the figures on every report if altered later?

  1. The accounting method
  2. The company logo
  3. The invoice colour
  4. The user's password
Show answer

Answer: A. Switching between cash and accrual restates income and expenses across all reports.

What does a closing date do?

  1. Prevents edits to transactions before that date
  2. Deletes old transactions
  3. Ends the subscription
  4. Closes the bank account
Show answer

Answer: A. It locks the period so reconciled figures cannot be quietly changed.

Where is the first month of the fiscal year set?

  1. Advanced settings
  2. Sales settings
  3. Payments settings
  4. The dashboard
Show answer

Answer: A. Fiscal year, accounting method and closing date all live under Advanced.

Why set default payment terms in Sales settings?

  1. So every invoice consistently shows when payment is due
  2. To change the tax rate
  3. To add users
  4. To connect the bank
Show answer

Answer: A. Default terms make due dates and overdue reporting consistent across all invoices.

Short answer

Name four settings that should be fixed before entering transactions.

Model answer

Accounting method, first month of the fiscal year, default payment terms and the company's legal details.

Why is a closing date important for trust in the accounts?

Model answer

Because once a period is reconciled and reported, locking it stops anyone from silently altering figures that have already been relied upon.

Class Activity

  1. Open Account and settings in a sample file and list one setting from each tab that would matter to a small shop.
  2. Decide the accounting method and fiscal year for an organisation you know and justify both.

Assignment

Produce a completed settings plan for a small organisation: state the value you would set for at least eight settings and give a one-line reason for each.

Printable: use your browser’s Print → Save as PDF to keep an offline copy.

lessons.title: 2.2 Entering Business Information
lessons.html:
QuickBooks AccountingModule 2: Setting Up Your Company File

LESSON NOTE: ENTERING BUSINESS INFORMATION

SubjectTopicLevelLesson duration
QuickBooks AccountingEntering Business InformationBeginner to Advanced30 minutes

Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you should be able to:

  • Record the legal and contact details of the organisation
  • Explain where each detail appears to customers
  • Add a logo and tax identification correctly

1. Introduction

The Company tab is small but public: almost everything in it is printed on the documents your customers, donors and tax authority will see.

2. What goes where

FieldAppears onWhy it matters
Company nameInvoices, statements, reportsMust match your registration to be accepted as evidence
Legal nameTax filingsMay differ from your trading name
AddressInvoices and statementsDetermines tax jurisdiction in some settings
EmailInvoices sent to customersWhere customer replies go
Phone / websiteInvoice footerMakes it easy for customers to pay or query
Tax number / TINInvoicesOften legally required for a valid tax invoice
LogoInvoices, estimatesProfessional credibility

3. Trading name vs legal name

Many organisations trade under one name and are registered under another. QuickBooks holds both. Put the name customers know on Company name and the registered name on Legal name; tax forms use the legal name.

Example: Registered as 'Tolbert Ventures Incorporated', trading as 'Tolbert Hardware'. Customers see Tolbert Hardware; the tax return says Tolbert Ventures Incorporated.

4. Common mistakes

  • Leaving the tax number blank, which can make an invoice invalid for the customer's tax claim.
  • Using a personal email, so replies to invoices go to someone who has left.
  • Uploading a huge logo file that makes invoices slow to load on a phone.

Summary

  • Company details are printed on customer-facing documents, so accuracy is a business issue not an admin one.
  • Trading name and legal name are stored separately and used for different purposes.
  • A missing tax number can invalidate an invoice for the customer.

Key Terms

TermMeaning
Legal nameThe registered name of the organisation, used on tax filings.
Trading nameThe name the organisation is known by publicly.
TINTax Identification Number issued by the tax authority.

Review Questions

Multiple choice

Why must the tax number be entered?

  1. A missing tax number can make an invoice invalid for the customer's tax claim
  2. It changes the subscription price
  3. It sets the fiscal year
  4. It adds users
Show answer

Answer: A. Many jurisdictions require the supplier's tax number for a valid tax invoice.

What is the difference between legal name and company name in QuickBooks?

  1. Legal name is the registered name used on tax filings; company name is the public trading name
  2. They are identical fields
  3. Legal name appears on invoices only
  4. Company name is used for payroll only
Show answer

Answer: A. QuickBooks stores both because they serve different audiences.

Why avoid using a personal email in company settings?

  1. Replies to invoices would go to an individual who may leave the organisation
  2. Personal emails cannot send invoices
  3. It doubles the subscription cost
  4. It disables reports
Show answer

Answer: A. The email is public on invoices, so it should belong to the organisation.

Which of these is a genuine risk of uploading a very large logo file?

  1. Invoices become slow to load, especially on phones
  2. The logo will not print
  3. QuickBooks deletes the file
  4. Tax cannot be calculated
Show answer

Answer: A. Oversized images slow down document rendering for recipients on limited data.

Short answer

List four company details that appear on a customer invoice.

Model answer

Company name, address, contact email or phone, and the tax number, plus the logo.

When would the legal name and trading name differ?

Model answer

When an organisation is registered under one name but trades publicly under another brand name.

Class Activity

  1. Write out the full company details you would enter for an organisation you know, including both names.
  2. Look at any invoice you have received and list which of these fields the supplier filled in.

Assignment

Design the company information block for an organisation of your choice and explain, field by field, why each entry is correct and who relies on it.

Printable: use your browser’s Print → Save as PDF to keep an offline copy.

lessons.title: 2.3 Setting Your Fiscal Year
lessons.html:
QuickBooks AccountingModule 2: Setting Up Your Company File

LESSON NOTE: SETTING YOUR FISCAL YEAR

SubjectTopicLevelLesson duration
QuickBooks AccountingSetting Your Fiscal YearBeginner to Advanced30 minutes

Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you should be able to:

  • Set the first month of the fiscal year
  • Explain how the fiscal year affects reports
  • Distinguish fiscal year from tax year

1. Introduction

The fiscal year tells QuickBooks where to start counting. Every annual report, every year-to-date figure and the year-end closing entry all depend on it.

2. Meaning

Fiscal year: The twelve-month period an organisation uses for its financial reporting. It need not run January to December.

Set it in Gear → Account and settings → Advanced → Accounting → First month of fiscal year.

3. Why it matters

Affected by fiscal yearHow
Profit and Loss for 'this fiscal year'Determines the start date of the period
Year-to-date figuresCounted from the first month you set
Retained earnings roll-overProfit is closed to equity at fiscal year end
BudgetsBuilt around the fiscal year

4. Fiscal year vs tax year

They are often the same but not always. The fiscal year is your reporting choice; the tax year is set by the tax authority. QuickBooks holds both separately under Advanced, so a school running July–June for reporting can still file taxes on a January–December basis.

Example: A school sets fiscal year start = July so annual reports match the academic year, while the tax year remains January.

Summary

  • The fiscal year sets where annual reporting begins and where retained earnings roll over.
  • It is configured under Advanced settings.
  • The fiscal year and the tax year can legitimately differ.

Key Terms

TermMeaning
Fiscal yearThe organisation's twelve-month reporting period.
Tax yearThe period the tax authority requires you to report on.
Retained earningsAccumulated profit carried into equity at year end.

Review Questions

Multiple choice

What happens to profit at the end of a fiscal year?

  1. It is closed into retained earnings in equity
  2. It is deleted
  3. It becomes a liability
  4. It is paid to the bank
Show answer

Answer: A. Year-end rolls the profit for the year into retained earnings.

Where is the first month of the fiscal year set?

  1. Advanced settings
  2. Sales settings
  3. The dashboard
  4. Banking
Show answer

Answer: A. It lives under Account and settings → Advanced → Accounting.

Can the fiscal year differ from the tax year?

  1. Yes, reporting and tax periods can legitimately differ
  2. No, they must always match
  3. Only for charities
  4. Only in QuickBooks Desktop
Show answer

Answer: A. Reporting periods are a management choice; the tax year is set by the authority.

A school wants annual reports to match its academic year starting in July. What should it set?

  1. First month of fiscal year = July
  2. First month of fiscal year = January
  3. Nothing; it is automatic
  4. The closing date to July
Show answer

Answer: A. Setting the fiscal year start to July aligns reporting with the academic year.

Short answer

Give one reason an organisation might not use a January–December fiscal year.

Model answer

Its natural business cycle may differ — for example a school aligning with the academic year, or a farm aligning with the harvest.

What is the effect of setting the fiscal year wrongly?

Model answer

Annual and year-to-date reports cover the wrong months, and profit rolls into retained earnings at the wrong point.

Class Activity

  1. Set the fiscal year in a sample company and run a Profit and Loss for 'this fiscal year' before and after; note the difference.
  2. Identify the natural fiscal year for three different kinds of organisation and justify each.

Assignment

Explain, with an example organisation, how choosing the wrong fiscal year start would distort its annual reporting, and state how you would correct it.

Printable: use your browser’s Print → Save as PDF to keep an offline copy.

lessons.title: 2.4 Multi-Currency Setup
lessons.html:
QuickBooks AccountingModule 2: Setting Up Your Company File

LESSON NOTE: MULTI-CURRENCY SETUP

SubjectTopicLevelLesson duration
QuickBooks AccountingMulti-Currency SetupBeginner to Advanced40 minutes

Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you should be able to:

  • Turn on multi-currency and understand its consequences
  • Record a transaction in a foreign currency
  • Explain exchange gains and losses

1. Introduction

Multi-currency lets you invoice a donor in USD while your home currency is LRD. It is powerful and, importantly, irreversible — once on, it cannot be switched off.

2. Turning it on

  1. Gear → Account and settings → Advanced → Currency.
  2. Confirm the home currency — this is permanent.
  3. Switch on Multicurrency and accept the warning.
Note: Do not enable multi-currency 'just in case'. It adds a currency field to every form and complicates every report. Enable it only when you genuinely transact in another currency.

3. How it works

StepWhat QuickBooks does
Add a foreign-currency customerCreates a receivable account in that currency
Raise an invoice in USDRecords USD and the home-currency equivalent at that day's rate
Receive payment laterConverts at the rate on the payment date
Rates differPosts the difference to Exchange Gain or Loss

4. Exchange gains and losses

Exchange gain or loss: The difference in home-currency value caused by the rate changing between the invoice date and the payment date.
Example: Invoice a donor USD 1,000 when USD 1 = LRD 190, so LRD 190,000 is recorded. Payment arrives when USD 1 = LRD 195, giving LRD 195,000. The extra LRD 5,000 is an exchange gain — not extra income from the donor.

Summary

  • Multi-currency is permanent once enabled, so only turn it on if genuinely needed.
  • Each foreign currency gets its own receivable and payable accounts.
  • Rate movements between invoice and payment create exchange gains or losses, not extra sales.

Key Terms

TermMeaning
Home currencyThe currency your financial statements are produced in.
Exchange rateThe value of one currency expressed in another.
Exchange gain/lossProfit or loss caused purely by currency movement.

Review Questions

Multiple choice

What must you understand before switching on multi-currency?

  1. It cannot be switched off again
  2. It is free for one month
  3. It changes the fiscal year
  4. It deletes existing customers
Show answer

Answer: A. Enabling multi-currency is permanent for that company file.

Why does an exchange gain arise?

  1. The rate moved between the invoice date and the payment date
  2. The customer paid extra
  3. QuickBooks made an error
  4. Sales tax was added
Show answer

Answer: A. The same foreign amount is worth a different home-currency amount on a later date.

An exchange gain should be understood as:

  1. A currency effect, not additional revenue from the customer
  2. Extra sales income
  3. A reduction in expenses
  4. A bank fee
Show answer

Answer: A. It is purely the effect of the rate changing, recorded separately from sales.

What does QuickBooks create when you add a customer in a foreign currency?

  1. A receivable account denominated in that currency
  2. A new company file
  3. A new bank account at your bank
  4. A payroll record
Show answer

Answer: A. Each currency needs its own receivable so balances are tracked per currency.

Short answer

Why should multi-currency not be switched on 'just in case'?

Model answer

Because it is irreversible and adds currency fields and complexity to every form and report, even if you never use another currency.

Explain an exchange loss in one sentence.

Model answer

It is the fall in home-currency value of a foreign balance because the exchange rate moved unfavourably between the transaction date and settlement.

Class Activity

  1. Work out the home-currency value of a USD 500 invoice at two different rates and state the gain or loss.
  2. List which organisations you know would genuinely need multi-currency and which would not.

Assignment

An NGO receives grants in USD and EUR but reports in LRD. Explain how you would set up multi-currency, and show with figures how an exchange gain would arise on one grant.

lessons.title: 2.5 Adding Users and Permissions
lessons.html:
QuickBooks AccountingModule 2: Setting Up Your Company File

LESSON NOTE: ADDING USERS AND PERMISSIONS

SubjectTopicLevelLesson duration
QuickBooks AccountingAdding Users and PermissionsBeginner to Advanced35 minutes

Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you should be able to:

  • Add a user and choose the right role
  • Match permissions to the principle of least privilege
  • Explain why the accountant role exists

1. Introduction

Giving everyone full access is the most common control failure in a small QuickBooks file. Permissions are your cheapest internal control.

2. The user types

TypeCan doTypical person
Primary adminEverything, including billing and closing the fileThe owner
Company adminEverything except ownership transferA trusted manager
Standard (all access)All accounting, no user managementA bookkeeper
Standard (limited)Only customers, or only vendorsA sales or purchasing clerk
Reports onlyView reports, no data entryA board member or funder
AccountantFull access plus accountant toolsYour external accountant

3. Least privilege in practice

Principle of least privilege: Give each person the minimum access needed to do their job, and no more.

This is not distrust; it limits the damage of a mistake as much as of dishonesty. A clerk who cannot reach the chart of accounts cannot accidentally delete an account either.

Example: A shop with three staff: owner = primary admin; bookkeeper = standard all access; sales assistant = standard limited to customers only.

4. Adding a user

  1. Gear → Manage users → Add user.
  2. Choose the user type and, for limited users, tick the specific areas.
  3. Enter their email; they receive an invitation and set their own password.
  4. Review the list every few months and remove anyone who has left.

Summary

  • QuickBooks offers admin, standard, limited, reports-only and accountant roles.
  • Apply least privilege: minimum access needed for the job.
  • Users set their own passwords via an emailed invitation; review the list regularly.

Key Terms

TermMeaning
Primary adminThe single user who owns the subscription and can transfer ownership.
Least privilegeGranting only the access a role genuinely requires.
Accountant userA special free role giving an external accountant review tools.

Review Questions

Multiple choice

What does the principle of least privilege mean?

  1. Give each user only the access their job requires
  2. Give everyone full access for convenience
  3. Remove all users except the owner
  4. Give access only to accountants
Show answer

Answer: A. Least privilege limits the damage from both mistakes and misuse.

Which role suits a board member who only needs to see figures?

  1. Reports only
  2. Primary admin
  3. Standard all access
  4. Accountant
Show answer

Answer: A. Reports-only access lets them view without any ability to change records.

How does a new user get their password?

  1. They set it themselves from an emailed invitation
  2. The admin types it for them
  3. QuickBooks prints it
  4. It is the same as the admin's
Show answer

Answer: A. Users receive an invitation and create their own credentials.

Why is limiting a clerk's access a protection even if the clerk is honest?

  1. It prevents accidental damage such as deleting an account
  2. It speeds up the software
  3. It reduces the subscription cost
  4. It improves report accuracy automatically
Show answer

Answer: A. Restricting reach limits accidental as well as deliberate damage.

Short answer

Name three user roles and one person suited to each.

Model answer

Primary admin — the owner; standard all access — the bookkeeper; reports only — a funder or board member.

Why should the user list be reviewed periodically?

Model answer

Because people leave or change roles, and a live login for someone no longer involved is an open door into the accounts.

Class Activity

  1. Draw a table of everyone who touches money in an organisation you know and assign each the QuickBooks role you would give them.
  2. Explain in two sentences why you would not make the sales assistant an admin.

Assignment

Write an access-control policy for a small organisation using QuickBooks: list each role, the access it gets, and how often the list is reviewed.

lessons.title: 2.6 Importing Existing Data
lessons.html:
QuickBooks AccountingModule 2: Setting Up Your Company File

LESSON NOTE: IMPORTING EXISTING DATA

SubjectTopicLevelLesson duration
QuickBooks AccountingImporting Existing DataBeginner to Advanced40 minutes

Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you should be able to:

  • Import customers, vendors, products and transactions
  • Prepare a spreadsheet that will import cleanly
  • Check an import before and after it runs

1. Introduction

Almost nobody starts from nothing. Importing turns an existing spreadsheet of customers or a bank history into QuickBooks records in minutes — provided the file is prepared properly.

2. What can be imported

  • Customers and vendors (name, email, phone, address, opening balance)
  • Products and services
  • Chart of accounts
  • Bank transactions (CSV from the bank)
  • Invoices, in most regions

3. Preparing the spreadsheet

  1. Download the QuickBooks sample import template first and match your columns to it.
  2. One record per row; no merged cells; no blank rows in the middle.
  3. Dates in one consistent format.
  4. Numbers with no currency symbols or thousands separators.
  5. Remove duplicates before importing, not after.
Note: Fixing a bad import is far more work than fixing the spreadsheet. QuickBooks has no 'undo import' button for most data types.

4. Running and checking the import

StepCheck
Map the columnsEvery required field mapped to the right column
PreviewQuickBooks flags rows it cannot read — fix these in the sheet
ImportNote how many records it says were created
VerifyOpen the list and count; compare a few records against the source
Example: Importing 120 customers: the preview rejects 4 rows for missing names. Fix them in the spreadsheet, re-import the whole file, then confirm the customer list shows 120.

Summary

  • Customers, vendors, products, accounts and bank transactions can all be imported.
  • A clean template — one row per record, consistent dates, plain numbers — is what makes an import succeed.
  • There is no undo for most imports, so preview and verify carefully.

Key Terms

TermMeaning
CSVA plain comma-separated spreadsheet format used for imports.
MappingTelling QuickBooks which spreadsheet column holds which field.
PreviewThe stage where QuickBooks shows what it will create and flags errors.

Review Questions

Multiple choice

Why must you fix errors before importing rather than after?

  1. Most imports cannot be undone
  2. QuickBooks charges per import
  3. Imports are limited to one per year
  4. Errors delete existing data
Show answer

Answer: A. There is no general undo, so cleaning the file first is far cheaper than repairing afterwards.

What is 'mapping' in an import?

  1. Telling QuickBooks which spreadsheet column holds which field
  2. Drawing the office location
  3. Linking the bank account
  4. Setting the fiscal year
Show answer

Answer: A. Mapping connects your column headings to QuickBooks fields.

Which of these will most likely break an import?

  1. Merged cells and blank rows in the middle of the sheet
  2. Using the sample template
  3. Consistent date formats
  4. Plain numbers
Show answer

Answer: A. Merged cells and gaps stop the file being read as clean rows.

After importing 120 customers, what should you do?

  1. Open the customer list, count the records and spot-check a few against the source
  2. Nothing; the import is always correct
  3. Delete the spreadsheet immediately
  4. Run payroll
Show answer

Answer: A. Verification against the source is what proves the import actually worked.

Short answer

List four rules for preparing an import spreadsheet.

Model answer

One record per row; no merged cells or blank rows; consistent date format; numbers without currency symbols.

Why is the preview stage important?

Model answer

It shows which rows QuickBooks cannot read so you can correct them before any data is created.

Class Activity

  1. Take a list of ten customers and lay it out in a clean import template.
  2. Deliberately introduce three errors into that sheet and describe how the preview would report them.

Assignment

Prepare a customer import file for a real or imagined organisation with at least fifteen records, then write a short checklist you would follow before clicking Import.

lessons.title: 2.7 Connecting Your Bank Account
lessons.html:
QuickBooks AccountingModule 2: Setting Up Your Company File

LESSON NOTE: CONNECTING YOUR BANK ACCOUNT

SubjectTopicLevelLesson duration
QuickBooks AccountingConnecting Your Bank AccountBeginner to Advanced35 minutes

Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you should be able to:

  • Connect a bank or card account to QuickBooks
  • Choose the right start date for downloaded transactions
  • Handle a bank that cannot connect

1. Introduction

Connecting the bank is the single biggest time-saver in QuickBooks. Instead of typing every transaction, the bank sends them and you simply confirm where each belongs.

2. How to connect

  1. Banking → Connect account.
  2. Search for your bank and sign in with your online banking credentials.
  3. Select which accounts to link and which QuickBooks account each maps to.
  4. Choose how far back to pull transactions — usually the file's start date.
Note: QuickBooks receives read-only data. It cannot move money out of your account; the connection downloads transactions, it does not authorise payments.

3. Choosing the pull-back date

Pull from your start date, not from the earliest date offered. Downloading a year of history into a file that starts this month creates hundreds of transactions that duplicate your opening balance and take hours to delete.

Example: File start date 1 January. Connect the bank and pull from 1 January only — even though the bank offers 24 months.

4. When the bank will not connect

Many banks, especially outside the US and UK, are not supported. The fallback is manual upload:

  1. Log in to online banking and export a statement as CSV or QBO.
  2. In QuickBooks, Banking → Upload from file.
  3. Map the date, description and amount columns.
  4. Import — the transactions arrive in the same review queue as a live feed.

The rest of the workflow is identical, so nothing in this course is lost if your bank cannot connect directly.

Summary

  • A bank connection downloads transactions read-only; it cannot move money.
  • Pull transactions from the file's start date, not the earliest date available.
  • Unsupported banks can upload a CSV statement and use the identical review workflow.

Key Terms

TermMeaning
Bank feedThe stream of transactions downloaded from the bank.
Read-only accessPermission to view data but not to make payments.
CSV uploadManually importing a downloaded statement file.

Review Questions

Multiple choice

Can QuickBooks move money out of a connected bank account?

  1. No, the connection is read-only and only downloads transactions
  2. Yes, it can pay any bill automatically
  3. Yes, but only to vendors
  4. Only with a Plus plan
Show answer

Answer: A. The feed is read-only; it downloads data and cannot authorise payments.

How far back should you pull transactions when connecting?

  1. From the file's start date
  2. From the earliest date the bank offers
  3. From today only
  4. From five years ago
Show answer

Answer: A. Pulling earlier than the start date duplicates the opening balance and creates cleanup work.

Your bank is not supported. What is the correct fallback?

  1. Export a CSV statement and upload it to QuickBooks
  2. Give up on bank reconciliation
  3. Type nothing and estimate
  4. Change banks immediately
Show answer

Answer: A. Uploaded statements enter the same review queue as a live feed.

What is the main benefit of connecting the bank?

  1. Transactions arrive automatically so you confirm rather than type them
  2. It increases your bank balance
  3. It removes the need to reconcile
  4. It files tax returns
Show answer

Answer: A. The feed replaces manual typing with review and confirmation.

Short answer

Why is pulling two years of history into a one-month-old file a mistake?

Model answer

Those older transactions are already represented by the opening balance, so they duplicate it and must be deleted one by one.

Describe the CSV fallback in three steps.

Model answer

Export the statement from online banking, upload it under Banking → Upload from file, and map the date, description and amount columns.

Class Activity

  1. Download a real or sample bank statement as CSV and identify which columns hold date, description and amount.
  2. Write down the start date you would use for an organisation you know, and why.

Assignment

Document the bank-connection procedure for an organisation, including what to do if the bank is unsupported and how you would decide the pull-back date.

lessons.title: 2.8 Setup Checklist Before You Start
lessons.html:
QuickBooks AccountingModule 2: Setting Up Your Company File

LESSON NOTE: SETUP CHECKLIST BEFORE YOU START

SubjectTopicLevelLesson duration
QuickBooks AccountingSetup Checklist Before You StartBeginner to Advanced35 minutes

Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you should be able to:

  • Run a complete pre-launch checklist on a new file
  • Explain why each check prevents later rework
  • Sign off a file as ready for daily use

1. Introduction

This lesson pulls Modules 1 and 2 together. Before a file carries real transactions, everything below should be true. Ten minutes here saves days of correction later.

2. The checklist

#CheckWhy it matters
1Company name, address and tax number enteredThey print on every invoice
2Fiscal year start setFixes all annual reporting
3Accounting method chosenChanging it later restates every report
4Start date decidedDefines what is opening balance and what is a transaction
5Chart of accounts reviewedThe structure all reporting depends on
6Opening balances enteredWithout them the file starts from a false position
7Bank account connected or CSV route testedEnables the whole banking workflow
8Default sales terms setMakes due dates and overdue reports meaningful
9Users added with least privilegeYour cheapest internal control
10Sales tax configured if you charge itWrong tax on early invoices is painful to unwind

3. Proving the file is ready

Two quick tests tell you the setup is sound:

  1. Run a Balance Sheet as at the start date. It should show your real opening position and it must balance.
  2. Enter one test invoice and one test expense, check the Profit and Loss moves as expected, then delete them.
Example: If the opening Balance Sheet does not balance, an opening balance is missing or has been posted to the wrong side — fix it before entering a single live transaction.

4. Sign-off

Write the date, who set the file up, the start date and the accounting method into a short note kept with the organisation's records. When someone asks in two years why the year starts in July, that note is the answer.

Summary

  • A ten-point checklist covers identity, dates, accounts, balances, banking, terms, users and tax.
  • An opening Balance Sheet that balances is the proof that setup is correct.
  • Record who set the file up and with what settings.

Key Terms

TermMeaning
Pre-launch checklistThe set of checks completed before a file carries live data.
Opening Balance SheetThe balance sheet as at the file's start date.
Sign-offA written record that setup was completed and by whom.

Review Questions

Multiple choice

What is the quickest proof that opening balances were entered correctly?

  1. A Balance Sheet as at the start date that balances and shows the true position
  2. A profit and loss showing zero
  3. The dashboard being empty
  4. The bank feed connecting
Show answer

Answer: A. If the opening Balance Sheet balances and matches reality, the opening position is sound.

Why must the accounting method be settled before live data?

  1. Changing it later restates every report already produced
  2. It cannot be changed at all
  3. It sets the subscription price
  4. It controls user access
Show answer

Answer: A. Cash and accrual produce different figures, so a late switch changes history.

Which check is described as the cheapest internal control?

  1. Adding users with least privilege
  2. Uploading a logo
  3. Setting the invoice colour
  4. Connecting the bank
Show answer

Answer: A. Restricting access costs nothing and limits both errors and misuse.

Why record who set the file up and with what settings?

  1. So future users can understand why the file is configured as it is
  2. To satisfy the bank
  3. To reduce the subscription
  4. It is legally required everywhere
Show answer

Answer: A. A short setup note answers later questions about unusual but deliberate choices.

Short answer

List any five items from the pre-launch checklist.

Model answer

Company details; fiscal year; accounting method; start date; chart of accounts; opening balances; bank connection; default terms; users; sales tax.

What two tests prove a new file is ready for use?

Model answer

Run an opening Balance Sheet that balances, and post then delete a test invoice and expense to confirm reports respond correctly.

Class Activity

  1. Run the full ten-point checklist against a sample company and note which items are incomplete.
  2. Write the setup sign-off note for a file you have configured.

Assignment

Complete the ten-point checklist for a practice organisation, evidence each item with a sentence, and finish with a signed-off setup note.
