lessons.title: 📝 QuickBooks Setup Quiz
lessons.html:
Module 14: Assessments and GraduationAssessment

QuickBooks Setup Quiz

Complete this quiz, then review every answer explanation to strengthen your weak areas before moving on. These questions are new: none of them appeared in the practice quizzes.

questions.question: Why set default payment terms in Sales settings?
options: So every invoice consistently shows when payment is due
questions.explanation: Default terms make due dates and overdue reporting consistent across all invoices.

questions.question: Which of these is a genuine risk of uploading a very large logo file?
options: Invoices become slow to load, especially on phones
questions.explanation: Oversized images slow down document rendering for recipients on limited data.

questions.question: A school wants annual reports to match its academic year starting in July. What should it set?
options: First month of fiscal year = July
First month of fiscal year = January
questions.explanation: Setting the fiscal year start to July aligns reporting with the academic year.

questions.question: What does QuickBooks create when you add a customer in a foreign currency?
options: A receivable account denominated in that currency
A new bank account at your bank
questions.explanation: Each currency needs its own receivable so balances are tracked per currency.

questions.question: Why is limiting a clerk's access a protection even if the clerk is honest?
options: It prevents accidental damage such as deleting an account
questions.explanation: Restricting reach limits accidental as well as deliberate damage.

questions.question: After importing 120 customers, what should you do?
options: Open the customer list, count the records and spot-check a few against the source
Nothing; the import is always correct
questions.explanation: Verification against the source is what proves the import actually worked.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of connecting the bank?
options: Transactions arrive automatically so you confirm rather than type them
It removes the need to reconcile
questions.explanation: The feed replaces manual typing with review and confirmation.

questions.question: Why record who set the file up and with what settings?
options: So future users can understand why the file is configured as it is
questions.explanation: A short setup note answers later questions about unusual but deliberate choices.

lessons.title: 📝 Sales and Customers Quiz
lessons.html:
Module 14: Assessments and GraduationAssessment

Sales and Customers Quiz

Complete this quiz, then review every answer explanation to strengthen your weak areas before moving on. These questions are new: none of them appeared in the practice quizzes.

questions.question: Which field decides whether sales tax is charged to a customer?
questions.explanation: The customer's tax status controls taxability, alongside the item's own setting.

questions.question: Why are sub-customers a poor substitute for classes?
options: Sub-customers sit under one parent, while classes cut across the whole file
questions.explanation: Cross-cutting reporting across many customers needs classes, not nesting.

questions.question: A $150 invoice is raised. What happens to the bank balance?
options: It rises by the tax only
questions.explanation: Cash moves only when payment is received.

questions.question: Why include the customer's purchase-order number?
options: It lets their finance team match and approve the invoice
questions.explanation: Matching to a PO is often required before a customer will pay.

questions.question: Where do you manage recurring templates?
questions.explanation: The recurring transactions list lives under the Gear icon.

questions.question: What single question decides which form to use?
options: Has the money already been received?
questions.explanation: Timing of payment is the whole distinction.

questions.question: An estimate the customer declined should be marked:
questions.explanation: Marking it rejected keeps the pipeline figure honest.

questions.question: A customer owing $500 returns $120 of goods. What is the new balance after a credit memo is applied?
questions.explanation: The credit reduces the receivable from $500 to $380.

lessons.title: 📝 Banking and Reconciliation Quiz
lessons.html:
Module 14: Assessments and GraduationAssessment

Banking and Reconciliation Quiz

Complete this quiz, then review every answer explanation to strengthen your weak areas before moving on. These questions are new: none of them appeared in the practice quizzes.

questions.question: What is the recommended banking routine?
options: Short sessions two or three times a week, oldest first
questions.explanation: Frequent short reviews keep the file continuously accurate.

questions.question: Why is the feed described as read-only?
options: It can download data but cannot move money
It can only be read once
questions.explanation: The connection has no payment authority.

questions.question: A $400 payment covers stock and fuel. What feature do you use?
questions.explanation: Split codes one bank line across several accounts.

questions.question: What is the safest default for a new rule?
options: Leave for review so you confirm the coding
questions.explanation: Reviewing lets you verify the rule behaves as intended.

questions.question: The bank credited $995 against a $1,000 payment. Best action?
options: Match and code the $5 difference to bank charges
questions.explanation: Resolving the difference keeps the customer's payment intact and explains the shortfall.

questions.question: What does a completed reconciliation prove?
options: Records and bank agree, with any gap explained by timing
questions.explanation: It verifies completeness and accuracy of the bank account only.

questions.question: What prevents previously reconciled months from changing?
questions.explanation: A closing date locks the period against edits.

questions.question: What should you do before making any adjustment?
options: Investigate until the cause is identified
Ask the bank to change the statement
questions.explanation: An unexplained adjustment hides an error permanently.

lessons.title: 📝 Reports and Payroll Quiz
lessons.html:
Module 14: Assessments and GraduationAssessment

Reports and Payroll Quiz

Complete this quiz, then review every answer explanation to strengthen your weak areas before moving on. These questions are new: none of them appeared in the practice quizzes.

questions.question: What does saving a customised report achieve?
options: The same settings are one click away next time
questions.explanation: Saved customisations preserve date ranges, filters and columns.

questions.question: What is the difference between the cash and accrual basis on this report?
options: Accrual shows earned and incurred; cash shows received and paid
questions.explanation: The basis changes when items are recognised, sometimes dramatically.

questions.question: A balance still sitting in Opening Balance Equity means:
options: The file setup was never completed
questions.explanation: That account is temporary and should have been cleared at setup.

questions.question: Why is depreciation added back in a cash flow statement?
options: It is an expense that involves no cash movement
It is not a real cost
questions.explanation: Depreciation reduces profit without any cash leaving.

questions.question: Why save a customisation?
options: The monthly routine becomes repeatable rather than rebuilt each time
questions.explanation: Saved settings preserve dates, filters and columns.

questions.question: A sensible weekly scheduled report for collections would be:
options: The receivables ageing, sent to whoever chases debts
The Balance Sheet to all staff
questions.explanation: It reaches the person who can act, at the frequency the task needs.

questions.question: What should be done before exporting?
options: Set the report exactly as required
questions.explanation: Fixing layout in the source is faster than reworking it afterwards.

questions.question: The same finding appears three months running with no action. What does this mean?
options: Either the finding is not important or the reporting routine has failed
questions.explanation: Reporting without action is a cost rather than a benefit.

lessons.title: 🧪 Midterm Examination
lessons.html:
Module 14: Assessments and GraduationAssessment

Midterm Examination

Complete this examination, then review every answer explanation to strengthen your weak areas before moving on. These questions are new: none of them appeared in the practice quizzes.

questions.question: Why does the course suggest using a sample company file?
options: It lets you practise freely without damaging real business data
It is the only place reports can be produced
Real company files cannot record transactions
It is required before you can buy QuickBooks
questions.explanation: A sample file is a safe sandbox: mistakes there cost nothing.

questions.question: Why is QuickBooks often described as a shared language between an owner and an accountant?
options: Both can work in the same file, so the accountant reviews exactly what the owner recorded
Because it translates between different languages
Because accountants cannot use any other software
Because owners are not allowed to see the reports
questions.explanation: A single shared file means the accountant reviews and adjusts the very records the owner entered.

questions.question: Why do the accounting concepts transfer between the two versions?
options: Both record the same double-entry accounting; only the menus differ
Because Desktop is a copy of Online
They do not transfer at all
questions.explanation: The underlying accounting is identical, so skills carry across; only navigation changes.

questions.question: What is the risk of downgrading a plan later?
options: Some features and their data, such as inventory quantities, can be lost
questions.explanation: Downgrading can be restricted and may strip features whose data then cannot be kept.

questions.question: What does the business type affect?
options: Which equity accounts are created, such as Owner's Equity or Retained Earnings
questions.explanation: Equity is structured differently for a sole trader, a company and a non-profit.

questions.question: Which panel would you check to chase money owed to you?
questions.explanation: The Invoices panel shows unpaid and overdue customer invoices.

questions.question: You want to change how invoice numbers are formatted. Where do you go?
questions.explanation: Sales form behaviour is configured in Account and settings under Sales.

questions.question: Where can you see the exact debits and credits behind a saved QuickBooks form?
questions.explanation: Transaction journal reveals the posting QuickBooks made for that form.

questions.question: What makes a chart of accounts 'good'?
options: It is detailed enough to answer the questions managers actually ask, without unused clutter
It has as many accounts as possible
questions.explanation: Usefulness for decisions, not size, is the test.

questions.question: A delivery van bought for use over five years is which type?
questions.explanation: An item owned and used beyond a year is a fixed asset.

questions.question: What is the most important choice when creating an account?
questions.explanation: Type determines which financial statement the account appears on.

questions.question: Can an expense account be merged into an income account?
options: No, merging requires the same account type
questions.explanation: Both accounts must share the same type and level to merge.

questions.question: How deep should sub-account nesting normally go?
questions.explanation: Shallow nesting stays readable and maintainable.

questions.question: An opening balance is best described as:
options: The position carried in from previous records, not a new transaction
A sale made on day one
questions.explanation: It represents history brought forward, not new activity.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an 'Ask My Accountant' account?
options: A monitored parking place for genuinely unclear items
questions.explanation: It parks uncertain items visibly so they are resolved rather than mis-coded.

lessons.title: 🧪 Final Examination
lessons.html:
Module 14: Assessments and GraduationAssessment

Final Examination

Complete this examination, then review every answer explanation to strengthen your weak areas before moving on. These questions are new: none of them appeared in the practice quizzes.

questions.question: Why does matching keep ageing reports accurate?
options: Settled invoices drop off, so only genuine debts remain listed
questions.explanation: Only correctly applied payments clear invoices from the ageing report.

questions.question: Five $200 payments are banked together. What should QuickBooks show?
options: One bank deposit of $1,000 matching one statement line
questions.explanation: Grouping them produces a single deposit matching the statement.

questions.question: What should the deposit total match?
options: The physical deposit slip and the bank statement line
questions.explanation: The deposit is a banking event and must agree to the bank.

questions.question: A customer overpays by $2 in rounding and will not return. Reasonable treatment?
options: Write it off to a sundry income account
Keep it forever as a credit
questions.explanation: Trivial amounts are cleared to sundry income rather than kept indefinitely.

questions.question: Why run ageing weekly rather than monthly?
options: A debt found at 45 days is far more collectable than at 90
questions.explanation: Early action materially improves recovery.

questions.question: How can a small team make monthly statements realistic?
options: Send them as a batch to many customers at once
questions.explanation: Batch statement runs make the task practical.

questions.question: What happens to reported Sales when a bad debt is written off?
options: Sales are unchanged; the loss appears as an expense
Sales fall by the same amount
questions.explanation: Keeping sales intact and showing the loss separately is more informative.

questions.question: When should a vendor opening balance be entered?
options: Only if you owed them money on the file's start date
questions.explanation: Opening balances represent debts existing at the start date.

questions.question: Why do bills matter for cash planning?
options: They make future obligations visible before payment falls due
questions.explanation: Knowing what is owed and when is the basis of cash planning.

questions.question: A $350 bill is paid $200. What remains?
questions.explanation: Part-payment reduces the balance and leaves the remainder outstanding.

questions.question: When is an expense the wrong form to use?
options: When the purchase will be paid later — that needs a bill
questions.explanation: Deferred payment requires a bill so the payable is recorded.

questions.question: Bank shows $10,000 and QuickBooks shows $9,400 with $600 of uncashed cheques. What is wrong?
options: Nothing; this is the expected effect of unpresented cheques
questions.explanation: Timing differences of this kind are exactly what reconciliation resolves.

questions.question: Why is authorisation before commitment better than approval after?
options: It prevents unapproved spending rather than merely detecting it
questions.explanation: Prevention is the point of the control.

questions.question: You owe $900 and record a $150 credit. What should the next payment be?
questions.explanation: Applying the credit reduces the amount payable to $750.

questions.question: What makes an early settlement discount worth taking?
options: When the discount exceeds the cost of paying early
questions.explanation: It is a straightforward comparison of discount against the value of holding cash.

questions.question: What does an inventory item need that a service does not?
options: Quantity on hand, an as-of date and a cost account
questions.explanation: Stock tracking requires an opening quantity, date and cost.

questions.question: What is the main cost of tracking inventory unnecessarily?
options: Ongoing counting, adjusting and valuing work with no reporting benefit
questions.explanation: Inventory tracking imposes a real administrative burden.

questions.question: A customer returns goods on a credit memo. What happens to quantity?
options: It increases, because the goods came back
questions.explanation: Returned goods re-enter stock.

questions.question: Six bags at $8 cost are lost. What is the profit effect?
questions.explanation: The lost cost is charged to expense, reducing profit by $48.

questions.question: What should the Inventory Valuation Summary total agree with?
options: The Inventory Asset account on the balance sheet
questions.explanation: Both represent the value of stock held and must reconcile.

lessons.title: 14.2 Graduation Requirements
lessons.html:
Module 14: Assessments and GraduationGraduation

Graduation Requirements

To graduate and earn your TIH Certificate of Completion in QuickBooks Accounting you must:

  • Complete the core lessons in Modules 1–12, from getting started through closing the books.
  • Submit the practical projects in Module 13 (company setup, sales and invoicing, expenses and bills, bank reconciliation, payroll records, and month-end reporting).
  • Attempt the four subject quizzes and both the Midterm and Final Examinations.
  • Present your Capstone: a complete QuickBooks file.
  • Pass the final Certificate of Completion assessment.

lessons.title: 🏆 Certificate of Completion
lessons.html:
Module 14: Assessments and GraduationGraduation

Certificate of Completion

This is the final graduation assessment. Pass it to complete the course and unlock your TIH Certificate of Completion in QuickBooks Accounting.

questions.question: Selling with a non-inventory item instead of an inventory item causes:
options: No cost to be recorded, so gross profit is overstated
questions.explanation: Only inventory items post the cost side of a sale.

questions.question: The valuation total does not match the Inventory Asset account. Likely cause?
options: Something was posted directly to the Inventory Asset account instead of through an item
questions.explanation: Direct postings bypass item tracking and break the link.

questions.question: What should you do before finalising the first pay run?
options: Run a test pay run and check every figure
questions.explanation: A test run catches setup errors before money moves.

questions.question: How should payslips be distributed?
questions.explanation: Pay data is sensitive and must reach only the individual.

questions.question: How many pay runs a year does a semi-monthly schedule have?
questions.explanation: Twice a month for twelve months gives 24 runs.

questions.question: Why does the pay date matter beyond the payment itself?
options: Deduction due dates are usually based on it
It sets the employee's start date
questions.explanation: Statutory liabilities are generally due by reference to the pay date.

questions.question: Why is spending withheld tax on operating costs so serious?
options: The money belongs to the authority and remains payable in full regardless
questions.explanation: The liability does not disappear, and penalties usually follow.

questions.question: When are payroll liabilities usually due?
options: A set number of days after the pay date
questions.explanation: Statutory deadlines are typically fixed relative to the pay date.

questions.question: How often should payroll be reconciled to the accounts?
questions.explanation: Monthly reconciliation catches errors while they are still easy to fix.

questions.question: What is a leading cause of tax arrears in small businesses?
options: Treating tax collected as available income and spending it
questions.explanation: Spending the collected tax leaves nothing to remit at filing.

questions.question: What does filing frequency determine?
options: How often a sales tax return is due
questions.explanation: It sets the reporting period for the return.

questions.question: Where should an item's tax status be set?
questions.explanation: Setting it at the item level makes every future invoice correct automatically.

questions.question: What effect do credit memos have on the tax due?
questions.explanation: Credits reduce taxable sales and therefore the tax owed.

questions.question: What are the two distinct events in this lesson?
options: Filing the return and paying the amount
questions.explanation: Filing fixes the amount; payment settles it.

questions.question: Why lock a period after filing?
options: So later edits cannot make the accounts disagree with the submitted return
questions.explanation: A filed return must continue to match the underlying records.
